audit_notes.scope: HTTP surface only (backend/app). lunapath_ros imports the same domain layer directly and was NOT audited.
audit_notes.working_tree: Dirty in frontend/ only; backend/ clean at this commit.
evidence_sources: read-only HTTP probes against a running localhost:8000
audit_notes.response_fields_note: Every response_fields entry below was observed in a live probe or read directly from the response-construction code cited in evidence.

trap_fields.astar_metrics.total_energy_wh: Always null. Real energy is summary.total_energy_consumed_wh.
trap_fields.astar_metrics.total_shadow_hours: Always null. Real shadow is summary.max_continuous_shadow_h.

name_spaces.warning: The shadow cost component is named 'shadow' but its grid layer is named 'shadow_ratio'. Do not conflate.

capabilities.notes: WRITES STATE: publishes app.state.active_corridor, active_corridor_id, active_corridor_rover_id and appends to app.state.corridors (32-entry FIFO), main.py:722-735. Not a pure read. typical_ms is wall time from one live probe on a 500x500 grid, (60,60)->(440,440); observed range across 4 runs was 2840-4848 ms and the server ran under --reload, so treat it as an order of magnitude, not a benchmark.

Accepts rover_id but NOT weight overrides, so the breakdown always uses metadata['cost_weights'] (main.py:549). Non-finite contributions serialise as null, never inf/NaN (costmap.py:124-129). Pure read.

PER-CELL ONLY. There is no route-wide component decomposition anywhere in the backend: CostMap.explain has exactly one caller and it passes a single (row, col). To answer 'what share of this route's cost came from slope', the AI layer must call this endpoint once per waypoint and aggregate client-side, which is N requests for an N-waypoint route (485 on the reference route). Values are already weight-multiplied contributions, so they sum to total.

Re-running with perturbed weights works and is deterministic for a fixed input (two identical live runs: total_distance_m 3028.34, nodes_expanded 111770, both times). NO CACHING: the repeat run was not cheaper (4848 ms vs 2840 ms), so each perturbation costs a full solve. Weights are NOT normalised - resolve_weights only overwrites defaults, no sum constraint (cost_engine.py:51-63). Every call writes corridor state.

Runs all four MISSION_PROFILES (balanced, energy_saver, fast_recon, shadow_traverse). Does not write app.state - no corridor is published, grids_for_rover derives per-profile grids without storing them (main.py:1276). Safe read despite being a POST. PIXEL COORDINATES ONLY - unlike /api/plan it does not accept {lon,lat}. comparison.recommendation states its own limitation verbatim: 'Energy and shadow totals are not tracked in fast mode, so neither ranking is an energy claim.' A sibling route POST /api/plan-multi takes an explicit profiles[] list with the same result shape.

PARTIAL. Margin = limit - actual is derivable for max_shadow_h (h), max_energy_wh (Wh) and min_soc (0-1 fraction). Live example, balanced profile: shadow 40.0 vs 3.3154, energy 4000.0 vs 1457.53, soc 0.2 vs 0.7311. max_slope_deg.actual is always null because it is structural (enforced in search). TWO LIMITS: (1) only /api/compare and /api/plan-multi produce constraint_check - POST /api/plan never does, so a single planned route carries no margin data; (2) the log-barrier slack values are NOT available at any granularity - see the C-BINDING entry under 'unavailable'.

edges_rejected is populated on SUCCESSFUL runs too, not only failures - live probe on a successful compare returned {step_slope:25, lateral_slope:4928, thermal_barrier:0, slope_barrier:0, lateral_barrier:0} alongside a valid path. It is therefore usable to explain why a route DETOURED, not just why one was impossible. On POST /api/plan the same counters are present in astar_metrics.edges_rejected for successful plans; only the FAILURE case drops them. AVAILABLE ONLY VIA /api/compare AND /api/plan-multi, which return HTTP 200 and carry the failure inside results[] with metrics intact. POST /api/plan is the opposite: main.py:627-628 raises HTTPException(404, detail=astar_result['error']) and DISCARDS metrics, so the structured edges_rejected counters and nodes_expanded are computed and thrown away - see the C-INFEASIBLE entry under 'unavailable'. The error string itself is prose built by _no_path_reason(), e.g. 'No path found for NASA VIPER: 412 edges exceeded the 15 deg roll-over (cross-slope) limit; ...'. Do not parse it - read edges_rejected instead. No partial path is ever returned (path_pixels is []). This path could not be triggered live during the audit (the loaded grid is 84.0% traversable); verified by source read plus backend/test_pathfinder.py:92, backend/test_review3_fixes.py:102, backend/test_review4_fixes.py:152.

unavailable.reason: No endpoint scores a caller-supplied path or route. cost_engine.total_edge_cost() implements the full weighted+barrier edge cost but no HTTP route calls it; the only way to price a path is to let the planner produce one.

Log-barrier slack values are computed but never retained. In every one of the four barrier functions the pattern is identical: compute slack as a local, pass it straight into math.log(), append to a terms list, sum, return a single float. slack_slope, slack_lat, slack_soc, slack_cold and slack_hot never leave their function. When a slack reaches zero the function returns inf, so even the identity of the binding constraint is lost. The only exposed aggregate is astar_metrics.barrier_share, a single ratio with no per-constraint breakdown.

POST /api/plan does not run check_profile_constraints, so a single planned route carries no limit/actual pairs. _attach_constraint_check exists and is called only from /api/plan-multi and /api/compare.

On POST /api/plan the structured failure diagnosis is discarded. _empty_result carries edges_rejected and nodes_expanded inside metrics, but main.py reads only astar_result['error'] and puts that prose string in a 404 detail. The response body is {'detail': '<sentence>'} with no structured field and no partial path.

No route-wide cost decomposition. Per-edge component penalties are summed into a scalar and discarded; nothing accumulates a per-component total along the path. CostMap.explain is per-cell and has a single caller passing one (row, col).
